title: Genetically modified and transgenic organisms
log: 2026-11-01T14:46:35Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The closest bank point teaches recombinant DNA and transgenic organisms, which is related but not the new point's idea: it never defines a GMO as an organism with altered DNA, and its questions test enzymes rather than the GMO-versus-transgenic distinction, so a new point is the safer choice.

draft.title: GMOs and transgenic organisms
card: a genetically modified organism. Its DNA has been altered by scientists, for example by adding, removing or changing a gene.
an organism that carries a gene from another species. The added gene is called a transgene.
All transgenic organisms are GMOs, because adding a gene alters their DNA. Not every GMO is transgenic: a gene can be changed or switched off without adding DNA from another species.
An example is a crop given a gene from a bacterium that makes a protein harmful to pest insects. The crop is then resistant to those pests.
draft.remember: A GMO has altered DNA. A transgenic organism also carries a gene from another species.

a.q: Which statement correctly links the terms GMO and transgenic organism?
opts: Every transgenic organism is a GMO
Every GMO is a transgenic organism
They mean exactly the same thing
a.why: Adding a gene from another species alters the DNA, so a transgenic organism is always a GMO. The reverse is not true, because a GMO can have its own gene changed or removed without any foreign gene.
a.clue: Does adding a foreign gene alter the DNA?

b.q: Scientists in Queensland switch off one of a tomato plant's own genes. No DNA from another species is added. How is the plant best described?
b.why: The plant's DNA was altered, so it is a GMO. No gene from another species was added, so it is not transgenic. Calling it transgenic is tempting, but that needs a foreign gene.
b.clue: Was a gene from another species added?

a.best: Every transgenic organism is a GMO
